title: Field Maple: Ancient Field Maples You Can Visit
meta_description: Europe's hedgerow maple, more often clipped than left to grow. Copenhagen's in Hans Tavsens Park is 4.03 metres round.
intro: Field maple is the tree that fills gaps between hedgerows rather than anchoring a park, usually clipped into a hedge long before it can become anything, so a big one stands out from its own species. Copenhagen's in Hans Tavsens Park has 4.03 metres of trunk, and the Danish register ranks it third thickest in the country. In Gdansk, the city council protected a pair in Park Oliwski in February 2026 and named them after Hugo Conwentz, the botanist credited with founding the world's first state conservation office. Utrecht's, on the Bartholomeibrug, is the only maple native to the Netherlands among all the city's maples. Prague's, in the Seminary Garden above a pond, carries a careful estimate of 160 to 170 years, and Graz has protected one in the Augarten since 1979, after a 1956 survey had already called it worth keeping.
